_llm_instructions: Fill in the 'project_title' and 'date_prepared' properties, and the 'value' property of each field, based on the provided project context. Reference parameters.md for global project variables. Record the date of measurement alongside every actual value: a figure measured early in the period and carried forward as final is the usual way a shortfall is reported as success, and the date is the only thing that distinguishes the two.

f01_Register_Purpose.label: Register Purpose
f01_Register_Purpose.guidance: What this register is tracking and which benefits it covers. State the scope, because a register that silently omits a benefit reads as a benefit that was never claimed, and the two are indistinguishable to a later reader.

f02_Reporting_Period.label: Reporting Period
f02_Reporting_Period.guidance: The period the entries cover and the date the register was last updated. Without a date a register of moving values is indistinguishable from one that was abandoned, and the two look identical on the page.

f03_Source_Documents.label: Source Documents
f03_Source_Documents.guidance: The business case and benefits management plan the entries derive from. The register does not create benefits; it tracks benefits defined elsewhere, and the source is what lets a reader check a target against the case that authorised it.

f04_Entry_Rules.label: Entry Rules
f04_Entry_Rules.guidance: What qualifies for an entry, and what does not. A register that accumulates everything makes no claim on anyone's attention, and the entries that get reviewed are then the ones that were easiest to write.

f05_Benefit_ID.label: Benefit ID
f05_Benefit_ID.guidance: The identifier for the benefit, matching the benefits management plan. Without a shared identifier the register cannot be reconciled against the plan, and a benefit can be tracked in one and dropped from the other without anyone deciding to drop it.

f06_Benefit_Description.label: Benefit Description
f06_Benefit_Description.guidance: The benefit as a measurable change, restated in the form it will be measured. The register is where a benefit written in prose has to become a number, so the description must be the one the measure actually refers to.

f07_Benefit_Owner.label: Benefit Owner
f07_Benefit_Owner.guidance: The role accountable for realising the benefit, which is normally not the project manager. The project manager can report the value; only the operating role can change the practice the value depends on.

f08_Measurement_Method.label: Measurement Method
f08_Measurement_Method.guidance: How the value is calculated, stated so two people would compute it the same way. Most disputes about a realised value turn on method rather than on the outcome, and an unstated method invites whichever reading suits the reader.

f09_Baseline_Value.label: Baseline Value
f09_Baseline_Value.guidance: The value the measure stood at before the project. Without it the actual figure has nothing to be compared against, and the register becomes a list of numbers rather than evidence of change.

f10_Target_Value_and_Date.label: Target Value and Date
f10_Target_Value_and_Date.guidance: The value expected and the date it is expected by. A target without a date cannot be late, and an undated target is met every day it goes unexamined.

f11_Actual_Value_and_Date.label: Actual Value and Date
f11_Actual_Value_and_Date.guidance: The value measured and the date it was measured. The date of measurement matters as much as the figure, because a value measured early in the year and reported as final is the most common way a shortfall is reported as success.

f12_Variance.label: Variance
f12_Variance.guidance: The difference between actual and target, signed. This is the column the register exists to produce, and a register that records only the actuals has omitted the only figure anyone reads.

f13_Status.label: Status
f13_Status.guidance: Where the benefit stands against its plan. The status should follow a stated rule rather than a judgement, since a status chosen to match the reporting is a status that reports nothing.

f14_Variance_Explanation.label: Variance Explanation
f14_Variance_Explanation.guidance: Why the actual differs from the target, recorded as a cause rather than as a gap. A variance with no cause cannot be acted on, and a benefit that is off plan for a reason nobody has established will stay off plan for a reason nobody has established.

f15_Corrective_Action.label: Corrective Action
f15_Corrective_Action.guidance: What is being done, by whom, and by when. An action without an owner is a note, and notes appear in the next version of the register as unresolved.

f16_Escalation_Trigger.label: Escalation Trigger
f16_Escalation_Trigger.guidance: The event that requires the benefit to be escalated rather than adjusted. Without a trigger the variance is absorbed at each review until it is no longer a variance but the plan, and the plan has quietly become the record of what happened.

f17_Benefit_Withdrawal.label: Benefit Withdrawal
f17_Benefit_Withdrawal.guidance: The grounds for removing a benefit from the register. Without them benefits are never withdrawn, only left at their last reported value, and a withdrawn benefit and a stalled one look the same forever.
